title: Trump, Xi and Putin issue 'Declaration towards Peace' after first three-way summit
dek: The four-point text reaffirms that a nuclear war 'cannot be won', promises a nuclear-risk dialogue, UN reform and more refined-fuel supply, and warns the ICC; it says nothing on Ukraine or Iran.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin issued a joint "Declaration towards Peace" after the first three-way meeting of the leaders of the three powers, in Shenzhen on Thursday, reaffirming that a nuclear war "cannot be won and must never be fought" and agreeing to hold a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The four-point text, released by the Kremlin and Chinese state media, also commits the three to reform the United Nations, to raise the production and supply of refined petroleum products, and to resist what it calls abuse of jurisdiction by the International Criminal Court.

The declaration does not mention Ukraine, Iran or the Strait of Hormuz, the conflicts that dominated the build-up to the meeting, and sets no figures, timelines or arms-control limits. Trump left Shenzhen for Washington shortly after the talks without speaking to reporters, and the White House had not released the text or its own account of the meeting by Thursday evening IST, reports said.

## What the declaration says

The document, titled the "China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration towards Peace", has a preamble and four paragraphs, according to reports of the text released by the Kremlin and China's state news agency Xinhua.

- UN reform: as permanent members of the Security Council, the three commit to reforming the UN so that it can respond more effectively to global challenges and fulfil its core mission of peace and security. The text gives no detail of what reform it means.
- Energy: the three say they intend to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products "for the benefit of all countries", and reaffirm the importance of stable energy flows.
- International courts: state consent and respect for the immunities of state officials are described as "of paramount importance", and the International Criminal Court and similar bodies must not "abuse" their jurisdiction.
- Nuclear weapons: the leaders reaffirm that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and commit to a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the spread of nuclear weapons.

The nuclear sentence repeats the language of a January 2022 statement by the five permanent members of the Security Council. The ICC has an arrest warrant out for Putin over the deportation of children from occupied parts of Ukraine, which Moscow rejects; neither Russia, China nor the United States is a member of the court.

## What happened in the room

The three leaders sat at a round table at the Kylin Villa, a state guesthouse in north-west Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. Only the first ten minutes or so were open to the press. Russia's state news agency put the meeting at about 90 minutes, while Chinese television described it as hour-long. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters afterwards that the statement had been adopted and that the "atmosphere was good".

"We are really making history," Trump told the other two leaders at the start, according to reports, adding that "no peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement". Trump had said he wanted nuclear arms control at the centre of the meeting; speaking of nuclear arsenals, he said: "It's not an easy thing to do – give them up." China has repeatedly refused in the past to join arms-control talks with the US and Russia, whose arsenals are far larger than its own.

Xi called the meeting "positive, constructive and fruitful", and said that "when major powers clash, the world falls into turmoil", reports said. He did not mention Ukraine in his public remarks, and told Trump that the US must "do the right thing" on Taiwan. Chinese state media said the talks covered Ukraine, nuclear non-proliferation, the Middle East and the Korean peninsula.

Putin said the discussion had taken place "in a completely open atmosphere, which allowed us to understand one another better", that Trump appeared "genuinely committed to ending the war in Ukraine", and that he wanted three-way meetings with the US and China to continue, according to reports. He also accused Kyiv and European governments of not being ready to compromise, and said the three had discussed potential threats from artificial intelligence.

## Background

The meeting capped a day of separate talks. Trump met Putin for about 40 minutes in the morning, a meeting the Kremlin said was mostly about Ukraine, and then Xi for a little over an hour, after which he said the two had agreed that oil must keep flowing through the Strait of Hormuz and that Iran could not have a nuclear weapon. Xi had personally greeted Trump at Shenzhen airport, the first time as president he has done so for a visiting leader, reports said.

The summit came days after Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge to Crimea for the third time in a week, and as the US-Iran conflict around Hormuz continued: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that two more tankers had hit mines in the strait, a claim that has not been independently confirmed. Peskov said the Ukraine peace process was currently on hold.

## Reactions

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Berlin on Thursday for a meeting of the "coalition of the willing", hosted by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and attended by delegations from nearly 40 countries, where he was also due to meet Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and hear about the Shenzhen talks. His priorities, he said, were "strengthening our air defence, energy and financial support" and diplomacy.

Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Putin and Trump were committed to a peaceful settlement and accused European governments of trying to obstruct their dialogue, Russian media reported. Jonathan Eyal of the Royal United Services Institute, a London think tank, said that "the big powers dictate, the small powers suffer", and that Putin had gained an escape from pariah status while Trump gained "a photo opportunity he didn't need", according to reports.

## Why it matters for India

India was not part of the meeting, and no reaction from New Delhi had been reported by Thursday evening. Three of the four points touch Indian interests directly. India has long sought a permanent seat on a reformed Security Council; the three powers' commitment to "reform" says nothing about expanding the Council. The US and Russia have said they support a permanent seat for India; China has not.

A three-way nuclear-risk dialogue among the US, Russia and China would leave out India and Pakistan, though China's growing arsenal is the main nuclear concern in Indian defence planning. On energy, India imports most of its crude oil and is one of the world's largest exporters of refined fuels, so a pledge by three major producers and consumers to raise refined-product supply matters for both its import bill and its refiners' margins. The text's silence on Hormuz, through which a large share of India's oil and gas passes and where Indian seafarers have been caught up in attacks this month, leaves that risk unaddressed.

## What happens next

Putin leaves for an official visit to Tajikistan, and Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said further contacts could take place on Friday. The White House has not said when or whether the nuclear-risk dialogue will begin, or who would take part. The coalition-of-the-willing meeting in Berlin continues, and European leaders are expected to set out further support for Kyiv.
